subject: Throughput guarantee & verification plan for Dedicated GPU pool (commit negotiation)
messages:
From: Jordan Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput guarantee & verification plan for Dedicated GPU pool (commit negotiation)

Hi Olga (and team),

Thanks for taking this forward. We worked through the outline internally and want to get clarity on three things before we finalize the commit:

1) What exact throughput guarantees (tokens/sec and requests/sec) Redwood will commit to for a 1.5M token/month reserved pool?
2) How are latency SLOs defined per-request (p95/p99) when throughput is at or near the committed level?
3) What is the measurement methodology and test harness we will run to validate the guarantee during acceptance testing?

We'd like to align on pass/fail criteria and a mutually-scheduled validation window. Attached is a short CSV with our expected traffic mix.

Jordan Sullivan
Head of Platform
Acme AI
[Attachment: traffic-mix-expected.csv (CSV) 8KB]

----

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantee & verification plan for Dedicated GPU pool (commit negotiation)

Jordan — great questions. High level answers:

- Commit: for the 1.5M token/month band we can offer a committed sustained throughput of 225 tokens/sec (aggregate across the pool) with an optional burst floor to 350 tokens/sec for short windows. That maps to our conservative tokenization assumptions for the set of models you selected.
- Latency SLOs: baseline p95 <= 180ms for 512-token requests and p99 <= 400ms under steady-state at the committed throughput. If you need tighter p99s we can propose a higher commit band or dedicated latency-optimized instance types.
- Measurement: we propose a two-phase acceptance: a deterministic synthetic run (scripted token feed) followed by a randomized sampling run using a representative prompt set (we can use your CSV to seed). Acceptance criteria: 95% of samples meet p95 latency target, and p99 not exceed the listed bound. Failure would trigger credits as defined in the SLA appendix.

I've looped in Marcus for the commercial framing and Karthik for the exact verification steps and artifacts. I'll also attach a draft pricing PDF and a preliminary test-plan.

Thanks,

Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-commit-pricing-v2.pdf (PDF) 220KB]

----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme.ai>, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantee & verification plan for Dedicated GPU pool (commit negotiation)

Jordan — quick commercial note on discounts and packaging:

- For a 12-month reserved commit at the 1.5M token/month band we can offer a 20% baseline discount off list with a step-up to 25% if you commit to a 24-month term and enable automatic burst credits.
- The pricing PDF includes a tiered discount table tied to committed hourly-GPU equivalents; as you'd expect, the higher commit reduces the unit token price and unlocks a larger guaranteed burst buffer.
- If you need hard latency SLOs that we measure separately (for p99 <= 250ms), we treat that as a premium add-on; pricing there is tied to a higher dedicated instance mix.

We can carve out a short commercial appendix for Acme with two options: Cost-first (maximize discount) or Latency-first (smaller discount + low-latency instance types). Which do you prefer as your negotiating posture?

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

----

From: Jordan Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantee & verification plan for Dedicated GPU pool (commit negotiation)

Thanks — both useful. A couple follow-ups from procurement and infra: 

- Procurement wants the acceptance test to be operator-run by Acme but observed by Redwood; we need the harness and exact command-lines up front so our procurement/legal can sign off.
- Infra asks: during the synthetic run, do you account for KV cache warm-up? We observed that initial requests are ~3-4x slower until cache priming stabilizes; we need the measurement to reflect steady-state behavior, not cold-starts.

Also attached a short doc showing our desired sampling distribution (primarily short-chat + 15% long generation).

Jordan

[Attachment: acme-sample-distribution.csv (CSV) 12KB]

----

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme.ai>, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantee & verification plan for Dedicated GPU pool (commit negotiation)

Jordan — thanks for the examples. Below is a concise measurement plan you can hand to procurement / infra. This will be the canonical acceptance test we run jointly.

Overview:
- Two-stage validation (synthetic deterministic + randomized sampling) run from your VPC peered to our private test harness in your region. Total run duration: 3 hours (1h synthetic + 2h randomized sampling).

Synthetic deterministic run (1h):
- Goal: verify aggregate tokens/sec at steady-state.
- Method: fixed prompt feed with token lengths drawn from your supplied CSV, with a 10-minute warm-up phase (to allow KV cache to reach expected hit-rate). Measurement window: last 50 minutes.
- Metrics collected every minute: aggregate tokens/sec, requests/sec, per-request latency histogram (p50/p95/p99), KV cache hit-rate, GPU utilization per instance.
- Acceptance: 95th percentile of minute-aggregates must be >= committed tokens/sec (225 tokens/sec). Per-minute p95 latency <= 180ms and p99 <= 400ms.

Randomized sampling run (2h):
- Goal: measure tail behavior on representative prompts.
- Method: randomized selection from your prompt corpus; include 1 in 20 long-generation samples to simulate mixed workload. No warm-up for these samples is required, but we will remove the first 10 minutes as a stabilization buffer.
- Acceptance: 95% of sampled requests must meet p95 target; p99 across the sample must not exceed bound.

Reporting and dispute resolution:
- Redwood will publish raw test logs and a summary CSV to a shared Drive link immediately after the run.
- If Acme disputes the result, we will jointly run a third arbitration run within 7 calendar days with identical seed and operators.

Operational notes:
- We will provide the exact load generator container image (sha256:abcdef... not listed here) and a runbook with CLI flags. You will be able to run the harness operator-side while Redwood observes; alternatively, Redwood can run from our environment with network mirroring.
- KV cache warm-up is accounted for via the 10-minute buffer. Cold-starts (node replacement during a run) will be excluded from acceptance by mutual agreement.

Next steps:
- Olga: please confirm commercial option (Cost-first vs Latency-first).
- Jordan: confirm Acme's preference for operator-run vs Redwood-run and propose validation window dates.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: throughput-test-plan.csv (CSV) 28KB]

----

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme.ai>, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Throughput guarantee & verification plan for Dedicated GPU pool (commit negotiation)

Jordan — thanks for the fast turnaround. Based on Karthik's plan and Marcus's pricing choices, here's the recommended path to closure: 

1) Commercial posture: Cost-first (20% for 12mo) with a documented upgrade path to Latency-first at any 6-month anniversary (we'll define conversion credits).
2) Validation: Acme operator-run test, dates proposed: Aug 16 - Aug 18 (three daily 3-hour windows). We'll provide the harness, runbook, and shared Drive link for logs.
3) Contract and next steps: I'll send the redlined term sheet and a DocuSign link once procurement confirms operator preference.

If that sounds good I'll queue the contract draft and DocuSign for signature.

Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
